messages:
alex: incident-bot paged me for elevated connection resets and 502s in eu-west-2 at ~09:12 UTC. I'm seeing spikes in SYN_RECV and short-lived TCP sessions. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INC-2026-4012 - alert: spike in downstream 5xx and connection resets for /v1/stream (eu-west-2) - threshold breached (1m).
oncall-bot: @alex critical page at 09:12 UTC — you are the current infra oncall.
alex: initial checks: CloudWatch ALB target groups show healthy, but instances report many ESTABLISHED->CLOSE transitions. VPC Flow Logs show traffic from app subnets to NATs but return traffic denied by NACLs in 2c.
jamie: I rolled out a NACL change via infra-ci at 08:53 UTC to standardize ephemeral port ranges. It was supposed to be additive but I see a deny rule for TCP ports 1024-65535 in the new ACL for eu-west-2c.
maria: support: getting customer reports of dropped streaming sessions and "connection refused" errors. Affected customer subset includes streaming-heavy tenants C and D. Raising severity on customer tickets 5410/5411.
sanjay: joining. Can you dump the NACL rules?
alex: snippet:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c --query 'NetworkAcls[?Associations[?SubnetId==`subnet-0c2c`]].Entries' --output json
```
Output shows a DENY for TCP 1024-65535 rule number 100 (priority) on NACL associated to 2c.
elie: yikes. that will break ephemeral return paths. probably cause of asymmetric egress: app picks NAT in 2b but return hits NACL deny in 2c because subnets were remapped during a separate subnet re-tagging job last week.
jamie: confirmation: terraform PR #783 toggled a mapping variable and the CI job that reconciles NACL associations ran after tagging changed. I missed a guard that prevents replacement of the default allow. I own that.
incident-bot: severity escalated to P1. paging netops and SRE leads. Add postmortem tag.
sanjay: mitigation steps: 1) add a permissive NACL rule to allow ephemeral ports temporarily, 2) revert the offending NACL entry via CLI to avoid another TF apply, 3) validate conntrack state on NATs, 4) monitor customer error rate and roll back infra-ci job.
alex: I'm going to apply a manual entry to replace the DENY with an ALLOW with a high rule number so the TF change can be reverted safely.
jamie: propose CLI to insert allow:
```
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f1e2d --rule-number 110 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress false --rule-action allow
```
Run dry-run first.
maria: notifying customers: "We've identified a networking rule change affecting streaming connections in eu-west-2 and are applying an emergency fix; brief reconnections may occur." Sending update now.
support-bot: Posted interim status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-4012 — message queued to impacted customers.
jamie: adding the allow rule now to NACL acl-0f1e2d in eu-west-2c.
jamie: (react) added. rule 110 created at 09:20 UTC.
alex: traffic should start to recover. ALB logs show fewer ECONNRESET and partial streams resuming. Error rate dropped from 9% to 1.8% in 2c.
sanjay: still seeing some residual errors from existing connections; conntrack on managed NAT gateways can't be cleared — but for NAT instances we can `sudo conntrack -F`.
elie: note: there are NAT instances in 2c for legacy tenants; NAT gateway for managed path unaffected. For NAT instances, flushing conntrack will drop active sessions but speed recovery.
sanjay: starting conntrack flush on nat-legacy-2c-01 after announcing to the channel.
jamie: executing now. `sudo conntrack -F` returns flushed entries count ~28k. expect brief reconnects for long-lived streams.
alex: immediate drop in error rate post-flush; most customers reconnected automatically.
maria: customers updated at 09:35 UTC: mitigation applied; we are monitoring. Support asked impacted customers to test and report lingering issues.
incident-bot: config-change detected: manual NACL entry added by jamie at 09:20 UTC.
jamie: root cause thread: two independent changes converged: 1) subnet tag-driven mapping changed which caused some app subnets to attach to eu-west-2c ACL, 2) infra-ci NACL rollouts included a deny rule (mistakenly) that blocked ephemeral responses. Combined produced asymmetric returns and stream resets.
sanjay: immediate action items: revert the deny rule in TF and lock NACL rule sets behind a guarded pipeline; add an automated post-apply invariant check that verifies ephemeral port coverage per subnet; add alerts for sudden spike in conntrack flush events or NACL denies per AZ.
elie: ops note: document which tenants use legacy NAT instances vs managed NAT gateways; consider migrating legacy NATs to gateway-backed path to avoid manual conntrack fiddling.
elaine: product: impacted customers are primarily those using streaming SDK v2. Please include a customer-facing summary and timeline in the postmortem.
maria: final customer update at 10:05 UTC: "The root cause was a network ACL rule applied during an automated rollout combined with a subnet mapping change. We have applied a fix and are monitoring; if you see reconnects beyond a 15 minute window, contact support."
incident-bot: incident INC-2026-4012 marked mitigated at 10:06 UTC. Follow-ups created: #NETOPS-102 (migrate legacy NATs), #INFRA-401 (TF NACL guard), #SRE-77 (post-apply subnet/invariant check).
jamie: I'll own the TF revert and pipeline guard. PR coming with approval required from netops.
sanjay: I'll lead the postmortem write-up and link the automation logs and conntrack dumps. Handing off to evening oncall at 18:00 UTC.
alex: thanks everyone. keeping the channel for any late customer reopenings.
maria: closing incident channel note: monitoring for 2 hours of stable traffic then we'll mark resolved on status page.
support-bot: Customers notified of incident resolution and postmortem promise.
